reviewedBy: analyst desk review (Phase 3) - NOT an expert panel and NOT participant cognitive interviews

vocabulary.double_barrelled: asks about two things at once
vocabulary.absolute_wording: extreme words (always, every, almost as my own) that compress responses
vocabulary.leading_or_desirable: agreeing sounds like the reasonable or admirable answer
vocabulary.construct_overlap: close to an item of another facet; test discriminant validity
vocabulary.not_true_opposite: keyed as the opposite pole but the two statements can both be true
vocabulary.sensitive_wording: phrasing that may read as a judgement about a person

items.note: Forced-choice comparison ("rather than"), not a pure agree/disagree statement; "theory" vs "checklist of facts" mixes abstraction with dislike of procedure.
Pairs with item 1 as a pole, but "trust" (epistemic stance) differs from "prefer" (activity preference); keyed opposite.
Clear, single idea.
"Happiest" adds an affect component beyond preference for the familiar.
items.proposal: I prefer to stick with what I already know works.

items.note: Clear. Close to the construct label "Panoramic".
"Tune everything else out" is extreme; and wide vs narrow attention are not logical opposites (a person can do both), so the pair may show weak negative aligned correlation.
items.proposal: I tend to concentrate on one thing at a time.

items.note: Clear. Self-insight item ("before I can explain it") is hard to verify but common in intuition scales.
Literal interpretation is a different construct from low pattern-sensing; wording can read as pathologising communication style.
items.proposal: I prefer information stated explicitly to reading between the lines.

items.note: "Decide quickly" and "adjust as I go" are two behaviours; overlaps with adaptability.
Reasonable. Overlaps conceptually with discipline/planning but keyed to decision timing.
Clear, observer-based rather than self-experience.
Expression vs concealment; "to myself" may also capture introversion (overlap with gregariousness).
Overlaps with R.tempo item 9 ("adjust as I go") and M.discipline; check facet correlations.
Near-duplicate of M.discipline item 35 ("systems and plans"); expect high cross-facet correlation.

Clear; "protect against the downside" is abstract for some readers.
items.proposal: I think about what could go wrong before I act.

items.note: Contrast clause ("not the crowd's") adds a second idea; socially desirable framing (independence).
items.proposal: I rely on my own judgment when deciding what to do.

items.note: Deference is less socially desirable to endorse; expect ceiling effects toward disagreement.
"Hard to move" fine, but the item measures stubbornness behaviour more than belief strength.
"When I hear a good point" makes agreement the reasonable-sounding answer; likely acquiescent/desirable skew.
"Stand apart" and "from everyone else" combine uniqueness with comparison; fairly extreme.
items.proposal: I like to be different from other people.

items.note: "Blend in" and "belong" are different aims (conformity vs affiliation); belonging overlaps with warmth and harmony.
items.proposal: I would rather fit in than stand out.

items.note: "Every situation" invites disagreement for almost everyone, compressing scores and creating a ceiling at the low end.
items.proposal: I behave much the same way in different situations.

items.note: Clear; "different person" is figurative.
Clear.
Keyed opposite to item 25 but "cool distance until earned closeness" also overlaps with trust and with introversion.
Clear. Pairs with item 28; nearest to extraversion, so expect overlap with warmth.
Clear, though "recharge" is jargon-light and common.
"Almost as my own" is extreme; endorsement will be rare and may measure emotional contagion rather than empathy.
items.proposal: I easily feel what other people are feeling.

items.note: "Head before my heart" is an idiom that may not translate; and cognitive-first processing is not the opposite of feeling others' emotions (a person can do both).
items.proposal: I tend to analyse a situation before reacting emotionally.

items.note: Clear. Smoothing over conflict is partly desirable, partly not; wording neutral.
"Hard thing" is vague (what hard thing?); mild desirability for candour.
"Always reaching" is extreme; combines ambition with restlessness.
items.proposal: I usually have a next goal in mind.

items.note: "Enough" is undefined; may be read as contentment (positive) rather than low drive.
"My life" is broad; overlaps with R.adaptability item 14 (stick to the plan).
items.proposal: I plan my days and weeks in advance.

items.note: Clear; contrasts "open" with systems, mixing spontaneity with disorganisation.
"Think big" and "want to build something large" are two statements; overlaps with M.drive.
items.proposal: I want to achieve something large.

items.note: "Enough, not grand" duplicates drive item 34 ("content once I have enough") almost verbatim.
Finishing is socially desirable; "even when it drags" adds a second condition.
Two behaviours ("chase what excites me" / "move on quickly"); overlaps with P.curiosity.
